svg.title: Key strategies to handle missing values — deletion
svg.desc: Reference card showing row deletion and column deletion methods, plus four important considerations before deleting data.

g.onclick: sendPrompt('When exactly is row deletion safe?')
g.text: Safe when < 5% of rows are lost

g.onclick: sendPrompt('When should I drop a column instead of imputing?')
g.text: Drop a column with too many nulls

g.onclick: sendPrompt('What is MCAR and why does it matter for deletion?')
g.text: Row deletion is only safe when data is MCAR.
If not, deletion introduces bias into your analysis.

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How does dataset size affect the decision to delete rows?')
sendPrompt('Should I impute instead of dropping an important column?')
g.text: Even with 60% missing, if a column is critical or target-related,
consider imputing rather than dropping it.

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How does deletion cause class imbalance in classification?')
g.text: Ensure deleted rows don't disproportionately remove one class.
Deletion shrinks minority class further → severe imbalance
